title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for colon cancer and liver metastases.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old male who presents for a follow-up evaluation regarding his current malignancy. He is currently receiving chemotherapy for a primary colon carcinoma. He reports some fatigue and mild abdominal discomfort but denies any acute fevers or severe pain. The patient is here today specifically to address the progression of his liver metastases. He states that the primary treatment is continuing as scheduled.

Medication List
Chemotherapy infusion (current cycle), Ondansetron 8mg as needed for nausea, and Multivitamin.

Exam
The patient appears stable and is in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness upon palpation. No hepatomegaly is noted. Skin is intact with no signs of infection.

Assessment
1. Colon cancer: The patient is currently receiving chemotherapy for this primary malignancy.
2. Liver metastases: The patient presents with metastatic disease to the liver.

Plan
Continue the current chemotherapy regimen as prescribed. We will monitor for any increased toxicity or systemic symptoms. Follow-up in two weeks to evaluate liver function and tolerate the current treatment cycle.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the colon under current treatment is a current malignancy: C18.9.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
